newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares mainly unchanged, outlook flat.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares mainly unchanged, outlook flat.

text.p: Norwegian shares were marginally lower on Friday in relatively thin volume and dealers said the market was expected to remain flat to slightly higher over the coming week.
Oslo's Total share index slipped 0.29 percent to end the week at 1,089.54 points. Almost one half of the session's turnover of 1.38 billion crowns was due to swap-related deals.
"There were no results out today, people were waiting for the U.S. payrolls data, all in all a very quiet day," noted one broker.
"But there are a lot of (first quarter) results out next week and Norway's inflation figure for April, I think we will hold around these levels or move marginally higher."
Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse accounted for 526 million crowns of the day's business as foreign investors opted to swap dividend for shares in a tax-related play, dealers said.

Turnover also was high at 124.8 million crowns in energy group Hafslund ASA, after one of its largest shareholders, Oslo Energi, opted to swap its B shares for A stock thus gaining more voting rights.
